title: Police car loses control: Responding FAST to emergency backup
description:
The incident occurred July 6, 2022 as a Spring Lake Park Police officer was responding to an "officer needs help call" in nearby Blaine, Minnesota. There were no injuries related to the crash and the Blaine officer needing emergency backup was also uninjured in the related incident. 

This video is exclusively obtained by MN Safety to promote transparency in government and encourage safe driving practices, including emergency vehicle operations (EVO.)

A thank you to the Spring Lake Park and Blaine Police departments for responding to our open records requests and providing excellent transparency as we examined the events leading up to the crash.

transcript.text: New video exclusively obtained by MN Safety shows a police car urgently responding to an emergency call, but losing control at a key moment. You'll see firsthand what happened, how it happened, and we'll do some investigative work to determine the speeds involved. At the end of this video, we'll show you a police squad rollover that happened on the same row just a few years ago, a quick visual reminder to all of us that we all can drive a little safer. But first, take a look as the Spring Lake Park Police Squad urgently responds to an officer being attacked or in a fight off Highway 65 in the North Twin Cities Metro. They're about to lose control of their squad at a key moment. That's the crash, and more to see on that in a moment. But first, just how fast were they going? Well, we can time how quickly they traveled from one intersection to the other, and then use Google Earth to figure out how far that is, and finally convert feet per second into miles per hour. Doing that, we get an estimate of 106 to 108 miles per hour as an average speed, but only for that section of roadway when they were traveling the fastest. So it's important to keep that in mind. As we get closer to the moment of the collision, you can see that they started to lose control as they went around the black SUV on their right. Thankfully, they were able to do significant braking over an extended distance, likely bringing their speed to under 35 mouth for hour at the point of end-packing. There's another one coming. One family recorded the scene, and they were kind of made fun of online by mean people, but I actually thought they did an excellent job. They had one person video record while another family member made the 911 call. They exchanged information between each other and discussed the best things to do. And importantly, they were careful not to make assumptions that the scene was safe. My car like locked up, man. Are you, uh, you're not injured at all, man? You're not injured at all? Sorry. This same roadway was the scene of another police squad involved crash, which is only to say that these types of high-speed arterial roadways, basically highways with stoplights, can be especially dangerous.
